claims.text: The initial single-crystal FeNiCrMn alloy has an FCC structure.
The initial alloy contains no pre-existing BCC phase or significant precipitates.
FeNiCrMn contains five principal elements, including an implicit fifth element or stoichiometric variation.
Random elemental distributions create lattice distortion and a fluctuating potential-energy landscape.
The fluctuating potential-energy landscape creates barriers to dislocation nucleation.
Yielding is initiated by thermally activated dislocation nucleation from the perfect lattice or defects such as surface steps and pre-existing jogs.
Local lattice distortion and temperature modulate the activation energy for dislocation nucleation.
A high nucleation barrier relative to thermal energy causes yield strength to be strongly temperature-dependent but only weakly strain-rate-dependent.
Yield strength decreases as temperature increases from 77 K toward 600 K.
Yield strength has minimal dependence on strain rate.
Dislocations nucleate at initial yielding without a detectable FCC-to-BCC transformation.
Crystal orientation significantly affects the critical resolved shear stress because lattice-distortion effects are anisotropic.
The yielding mechanism remains nucleation-controlled for both [001] and [111] orientations.
Traditional FCC metals such as pure Ni and Fe-Ni alloys exhibit greater yield-strength strain-rate sensitivity than the proposed HEA.
Traditional FCC metals have lower lattice distortion and different dislocation nucleation or propagation dynamics.
In polycrystalline samples, grain-boundary sliding or twinning may dominate deformation.
High Al or Ti content can intrinsically stabilize BCC phases.
Common Neighbor Analysis can distinguish atomic structures, and the Dislocation Extraction Algorithm can track dislocation motion.
Automated atomistic-analysis tools can be used to identify and analyze dislocation evolution.
Detection of more than 5% BCC before or concurrently with 0.2%-offset yielding would falsify the claim that dislocation nucleation, rather than FCC-to-BCC transformation, controls yielding.

contradictions.description: The alloy is repeatedly named FeNiCrMn, which specifies four elements, but the structural mediator calls it a five-principal-element alloy with an unspecified implicit fifth element, and the uncertainty field calls it a quinary composition.
The intervention states that strain rates span cryogenic to 600 K, although 77–600 K is a temperature range; the conditions field separately treats temperature and strain rate correctly.
